svg.title: One gradient-descent step on the single neuron, and the trajectory it starts
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure in two halves. The left card takes one update with a learning rate of nought point nought one: w nought goes from minus three to minus three point one two on a gradient of twelve, w one from minus one to minus nought point seven six on a gradient of minus twenty-four, w two from two to one point six four on a gradient of thirty-six, and the bias from one to nought point eight eight on a gradient of twelve. The pre-activation z falls from six to four point two and the loss from thirty-six to seventeen point six four, with a note that w one had a negative gradient so the rule raised it. The right card plots the loss over twenty iterations of the same step, marking thirty-six at the start, then seventeen point six, eight point six and one point nought, decaying geometrically towards zero and underflowing by iteration twenty. A band explains that each step scales the pre-activation by nought point seven so the squared loss is multiplied by nought point four nine each time, and that it approaches zero without reaching it because the gradient shrinks in lock-step with z.
svg.text: One update with α = 0.01, and what the same update does when it is repeated.
w₁ had a negative gradient, so the rule raised it.
iterations · by 20 the squared loss has underflowed to 0.0000
Each step scales the pre-activation by 0.7, so the squared loss is multiplied by 0.49 every iteration.
It approaches zero without reaching it: the gradient shrinks in lock-step with z, so the steps shrink too.
